subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-per-run by default, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` be rejected as a one-shot-only lifecycle flag?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode opposite product contracts, and the correct upgrade behavior for already-persisted omitted values depends on that choice.

options.title: Complete recurring cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, add persisted omitted-job handling or a doctor migration, and close or rework the strict-rejection proposal.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only validation
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict validation path after its caller, UI, docs, and recovery gaps are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land this PR as a limited default change while explicitly documenting that existing omitted jobs still need operator or doctor follow-up.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, add persisted omitted-job handling or a doctor migration, and close or rework the strict-rejection proposal.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron normalization and store work makes this the best available owner for the lifecycle-contract decision.
